To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the concept of work-integrated communities can provide a useful way of supporting learning and competence development in organisations, and that this is a way of supporting learning that is not only relevant in organisations, but also in schools and other learning environments.
work-integrated learning is a social activity that requires a holistic and integrated strategy.
WIL activities in organizations are best understood as a social process of learning and knowledge development in which the role of technology is to support the process of negotiation of practice.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of technology as well as the organisational context in which technology is used, in the development of WIL.
the question how learning in organisations can be understood and supported.
how to support the learning processes that occur in the workplace, as well as in the learning that takes place in organisations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
WIL is a means of supporting competence development and learning activities in organisations, but it is not a goal in itself.
WIL is a concept of learning that is situated in the context of work, but is not necessarily work itself.
work-integrated learning is a concept that can be used to support the competence development of individuals and the learning processes in organisations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have tried to develop a new conceptual framework for WIL and to demonstrate the potential of the approach by applying it on a real case.
the concept of WIL can be used to describe and support the activities of competence development in organizations.
we see a potential for a new way of thinking and acting in the area of work-integrated and collaborative learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
WIL can be understood as a means to support learning in organisations.
WIL is a concept that is not only relevant in the context of higher education, but that it also has potential to be used in the context of organisational learning.
WIL is not a one-size fits all approach, but rather a means to support the development of learning communities that are embedded in the context of work.
